sources.entry: How SRE teams are organized, and how to get started

summary.name: How SRE teams are organized (Google Cloud Blog)
summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud blog article describing six common ways to structure Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams, with their pros, cons, and recommended use, plus tiers of service and common SRE evolution paths.
keywords: how to start an sre team
use_cases: Deciding how to organize a new SRE team
Comparing kitchen sink, infrastructure, tools, product, embedded and consulting SRE models
Defining tiers of service for SRE engagement
Planning how an SRE practice evolves as a company grows
Writing a team charter to limit scope and overload
summary.what_it_does: The article describes six SRE team implementations: Kitchen Sink (everything SRE), Infrastructure, Tools, Product/application, Embedded, and Consulting. For each, it lists pros, cons, and recommended conditions. It also covers two modifiers: reliability standards and practices (influence versus mandates) and tiers of service (for example Tier 0 consulting, Tier 1 project work, Tier 2 on-call onboarding). It ends with common evolution paths and suggested next steps for teams starting or already running SRE.
notable: Compares six SRE team structures with pros, cons, and recommended contexts
Describes tiers of service as a way to avoid overloading SRE teams
Explains influence versus mandate approaches to adopting reliability standards
caveats: Describes Google's own observed implementations; the list is explicitly not exhaustive
Advises that GCP customers must apply through an account manager to request CRE involvement
